articles.headline: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
articles.description: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
articles.headlineJa: ブルズ、バディ・ヒールドと金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツへ放出
articles.descriptionJa: ブルズは、バディ・ヒールドおよび金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツに放出した。
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal. 

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans. 

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグの複数のクラブがトレント・アレクサンダー＝アーノルドの動向に注目しています。「Transfer Talk」が最新情報をお伝えします。
articles.body:
A group of Premier League clubs are keeping an eye on Trent Alexander-Arnold. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester City, and Chelsea are keeping tabs on Real Madrid right back Trent Alexander-Arnold, reports TEAMtalk. The Premier League clubs have been in contact with the 27-year-old's representatives, who have explored what options could be available should he leave the Bernabéu. Alexander-Arnold is keen to stay put with the LaLiga side this season which has made a potential move in January unlikely, though the situation is expected to be assessed at the end of the season.

- Juventus are interested in Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The Bianconeri are monitoring the 32-year-old's situation at the Etihad Stadium, where he is set to enter the final six months of his contract in January, and the Serie A club are ready to make an approach to sign him on a free transfer. Kovacic has played just two minutes of football in the Premier League this season across two substitute appearances.

- Bayern Munich are keen on Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, reports Bild journalist Christian Falk. The 24-year-old is said to have been on the Bundesliga side's radar for some time, but whether they push forward for a move for him depends on if they decide to part ways with center back Kim Min-jae. Araujo has been in impressive form so far this season, producing a standout display in the recent 2-0 Europa League win over AC Milan at the San Siro.

- Real Madrid are no longer looking to part ways with defender Raúl Asencio, reports Marca. The 23-year-old dismissed interest from Chelsea and Liverpool in the summer despite Madrid manager Jose Mourinho "showing him the door," and while he hasn't made an appearance in La Liga this season, the situation is now set to change after the injury to Ibrahima Konaté and recent red card to Dean Huijsen during the 2-1 league defeat to Atletico Madrid.

- Roma will demand an offer worth around €100 million should suitors return for midfielder Manu Koné, reports Gazzetta dello Sport. Two goals in the 2-2 draw with Inter Milan continued a promising start to the season for the 25-year-old, who Chelsea made a proposal worth around €60m for in the summer. The Giallorossi now want any potential offer to reflect his recent form and be comparable to Sandro Tonali's £100m switch from Newcastle to Tottenham Hotspur.

articles.headline: Sources: Caleb Williams injury considered to have 3-4 week timeline
articles.description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury that doctors say could sideline him for three to four weeks, league sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者情報：ケイレブ・ウィリアムズの怪我は全治3〜4週間の見通し
articles.descriptionJa: ベアーズのQBケイレブ・ウィリアムズはグレード2のハムストリング損傷を負っており、医師は全治3〜4週間と判断していると、リーグ関係者がESPNとNFLネットワークに語った。
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury that doctors say could sideline him for three to four weeks, league sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

This doesn't mean that Williams, whom the Bears have touted as a quick healer, couldn't return sooner than that timeline. It just means that doctors believe this type of injury normally takes three to four weeks of recovery and that is the doctors' best estimation of how long it could take Williams to recover.

The Bears ruled Williams out for their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night and have tried to keep the extent of his injury under wraps for competitive-purpose advantages.

But there also have been little hints that the Bears have dropped.

When Ben Johnson spoke with reporters Monday, after Williams underwent imaging on his hamstring, the Bears coach said the test results were "somewhat encouraging." Johnson also told ESPN 1000 radio in Chicago that Williams would be sidelined for "some time" before clarifying to reporters that the team was calling the quarterback's status week-to-week.

"Here's what I know," Johnson said at the time. "This guy's a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I'll double down on that. He gets back -- he has in the past -- a lot faster than what people can anticipate, and so I'm not putting a timeline on this. We're going to say week-to-week. He's going to attack this with everything that he knows."

To make matters more complicated for Chicago, backup Tyson Bagent reported to the team Tuesday that he was feeling the effects of a concussion and was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol, meaning third-string quarterback Case Keenum could start Monday night.

Bagent was still in the concussion protocol as of Saturday and is officially questionable for Monday's game, although he was a full participant in Saturday's practice. Keenum, 38, has not started a game since the 2023 season when he was with the Houston Texans.

Johnson said Saturday that the Bears are still determining their quarterback depth chart against the Eagles, including who will start.

"There's a different skill set, obviously," Johnson said. "One guy's a little bit more mobile than the other, and yet both are very cerebral players. I know they'll be mentally prepared for the game, and we'll see what it looks like. But there's a reason why Tyson was the backup as we ended camp, and we felt good about who he is as a player and what he can bring to the table to this offense."

As for Williams, he injured the same hamstring in college. Last week, the third-year star went down without contact in severe pain and was eventually carted off in the fourth quarter of Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

One reason for the pain was that Williams likely felt scar tissue breaking up from a past hamstring injury, a phenomenon that can be quite painful to experience but doesn't lead to long-term damage.

articles.headline: Sources: Cowboys, Lions make trade inquiries on Joey Porter Jr.
articles.description: A handful of teams, including the Cowboys and Lions, have begun making inquiries about the availability of Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：カウボーイズとライオンズがジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアのトレードについて問い合わせ
articles.descriptionJa: 情報筋がESPNに語ったところによると、カウボーイズやライオンズを含むいくつかのチームが、スティーラーズのコーナーバックであるジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアの獲得可能性について問い合わせを始めている。
articles.body:
A handful of teams, including the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions, have begun making inquiries about the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., league sources told ESPN.

The Steelers would be willing to listen to trade offers for Porter, according to sources, but they would want a strong compensation package if they were to deal the fourth-year star.

Porter has been seeking a new contract, but the Steelers do not negotiate deals during the season, raising questions about the possibility of a trade.

The Cowboys have aggressively overhauled their defense over the past 13 months, acquiring Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and Kenny Clark in trades while using first-round draft picks on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence.

But Dallas remains thin at cornerback, where Porter would potentially provide a significant boost. Cowboys starting cornerback Cobie Durant will not play in Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens because of a hamstring injury.

Another team that could use help in the secondary is the Lions, who have yielded the second-most passing yards in the NFL over the first two weeks of the season. Detroit is without injured safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, who are both on the physically unable to perform list, and cornerback Avonte Maddox, who is out for the season with a foot injury.

Porter has not played this season as he continues a prolonged "ramp-up" process to return from a back injury. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals after being limited in practice this week.

He said Thursday that he "definitely" would play for the Steelers in 2026 despite not getting a contract extension but was noncommittal about his status against the rival Bengals.

articles.headline: Giants set game plan with Jameis Winston, mull options to add QB
articles.description: The Giants' pursuit of a veteran quarterback will depend on how well Jameis Winston performs against the Titans in Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツ、ジェイミス・ウィンストンを軸に試合計画を策定　QB補強の選択肢も検討
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツがベテランQBの獲得に動くかどうかは、第3週のタイタンズ戦でジェイミス・ウィンストンがどのようなプレーを見せるかにかかっている。
articles.body:
Jameis Winston is in the spotlight Sunday in his first start of the post-Jaxson Dart portion of the 2026 season, and the New York Giants' next quarterback is expected to come into focus as early as next week.

QB2 is now QB1 for New York, and how hard the Giants push to acquire a veteran quarterback will be determined, in part, by how Winston performs Sunday against the Tennessee Titans.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said "all options are open" for which quarterback his team will bring in.

Sources told ESPN and NFL Network that the list of quarterbacks includes free agent Jimmy Garoppolo, Cardinals backup Gardner Minshew II, Vikings reserve J.J. McCarthy, 49ers backup Mac Jones and Chiefs backup Justin Fields.

Brandon Allen, who was in training camp with the Giants, is also a possibility.

Dart is out for the regular season after undergoing surgery Friday to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee, although Harbaugh did leave the door open for a possible return by the second-year star if New York makes a playoff run.

If Winston struggles again as he did against the Los Angeles Rams after being thrust into action in Week 2, the push for a new quarterback could be significant. Jake Haener was signed from the practice squad Saturday and will serve as Winston's backup against the Titans.

Winston was 11-of-27 for 111 yards with an interception in the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on "Monday Night Football."

There have been conversations with Garoppolo and his camp this past week, though he has not come in for a workout. He might be the Giants' most intriguing option, because signing Garoppolo would not require giving up a draft pick in a trade.

Garoppolo mulled retirement during the offseason but ultimately decided he is open to a return in the right circumstances, preferring to being on the 53-man roster -- instead of the practice squad -- if he does sign. The Rams wanted him back all offseason, and the Cardinals made a run as well.

But Garoppolo remains unsigned and is considering the Giants.

As for the others, Minshew played for Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy with the Chiefs, and Fields plays in the same system now in Kansas City. Jones is considered to be among the NFL's top backups, having gone 5-3 last year in relief of Brock Purdy.

McCarthy is intriguing because of his talent and because he is currently entrenched as Minnesota's third-string quarterback. The Giants have been doing legwork on McCarthy, making sure they can make an informed decision.

Will one of these names be necessary? The Giants feel like Winston played so poorly against the Rams, in part, because their game plan was tailored to Dart. Having to adjust to a pocket-passing quarterback like Winston proved a challenge. In addition, the silent count was an issue because Winston didn't rep it with them last week.

articles.headline: Sources: Raiders TE Brock Bowers expected to play vs. Saints
articles.description: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is expected to play Sunday against the Saints, barring a surprise, a source told ESPN
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：レイダースのTEブロック・バウアーズ、セインツ戦に出場見込み
articles.descriptionJa: 情報筋がESPNに語ったところによると、レイダースのタイトエンドであるブロック・バウアーズは、予期せぬ事態がない限り、日曜日のセインツ戦に出場する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is expected to play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, barring a surprise, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Coach Klint Kubiak said this week that he was optimistic about Bowers' return, and the Raiders did not elevate a tight end for game day like in previous weeks.

Bowers, who is listed as questionable with a knee injury, missed the first two weeks of the regular season after undergoing a meniscus trim procedure Sept. 8. He practiced on a limited basis Wednesday and Thursday this week before missing Friday's practice, which Kubiak said was planned.

Bowers has missed multiple games due to a knee injury for the second straight year. He suffered a posterior cruciate ligament injury and bone bruise in his left knee in the 2025 season opener against the New England Patriots, played three games with the injury and had to sit out for three games to return to full strength.

With Bowers out to start this season, Michael Mayer has been the top Raiders' top tight end for the first two weeks, catching nine passes for 55 yards.

Bowers, considered one of the best tight ends in the NFL, has caught 176 passes for 1,874 yards and 12 touchdowns over his first two seasons.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィークで負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は誰？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027シーズンの最初の代表ウィーク中に負傷したプレミアリーグのスター選手に関する最新ニュースと更新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.
